def create_folder(name, location='\\'):
    r"""
    Create a folder in which to create tasks.

    :param str name: The name of the folder. This will be displayed in the task
        scheduler.

    :param str location: A string value representing the location in which to
        create the folder. Default is '\\' which is the root for the task
        scheduler (C:\Windows\System32\tasks).

    :return: True if successful, False if unsuccessful
    :rtype: bool

    CLI Example:

    .. code-block:: bash

        salt 'minion-id' task.create_folder <folder_name>
    """
    :Example:

     >>> from win_task_scheduler import create_folder
     >>> create_folder('My Folder')
     True
     """
     try:
         task_scheduler.create_folder(name, location)
         return True
     except Exception as e:
         print(e)
         return False

def delete_folder(name, location='\\'):
    r"""
    Delete a folder from the task scheduler.

    :param str name: The name of the folder. This will be displayed in the task
        scheduler.

    :param str location: A string value representing the location in which to
        create the folder. Default is '\\' which is the root for the task
        scheduler (C:\Windows\System32\tasks).

    :return: True if successful, False if unsuccessful
    :rtype: bool

    :Example:

    >>> from win_task_scheduler import delete_folder
    >>> delete_folder('My Folder')
    True
    """
    try:
        task_scheduler.delete_folder(name, location)
        return True
    except Exception as e:
        print(e)
        return False


def get_folder(name, location='\\'):
    r"""
    Get a folder from the task scheduler.

    :param str name: The name of the folder. This will be displayed in the task
        scheduler.

    :param str location: A string value representing the location in which to
        create the folder. Default is '\\' which is the root for the task
        scheduler (C:\Windows\System32\tasks).

    :return: The folder object
    :rtype: :class:`Folder <win_task_scheduler.Folder>`

    :Example:

    >>> from win_task_scheduler import get_folder
    >>> folder = get_folder('My Folder')
    """
    return task_scheduler.get_folder(name, location)
